subject: Acme VPC pool: throughput gating and lane allocation
messages:
From: Alex Turner <infra@acmesystems.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <ops@devops-consult.com>
Date: 2026-08-01 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Acme VPC: initial throughput targets and network lanes

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for committing time to help us size the private VPC pool. A quick summary of where we are and what we need from Redwood: 

- Current on-prem hardware: 6 racks, each rack has 8x A100-80GB (we can add racks later).
- Traffic profile: attached CSV (acme-current-load.csv) — average token production ~75k tokens/min during business hours, peak bursts up to ~180k tokens/min (short spikes).
- Primary model: Acme uses a 35B decoder model with average generation length 160 tokens; 95th-percentile seq length ~512.
- SLOs: 95th latency target for interactive flows is 300ms; batch jobs can be >1s.
- Encryption: traffic will be over private link with mTLS + network-level encryption; we do not allow egress to public IPs.
- Network topology: see network-topology.pdf — we have two leaf switches per rack and a pair of upstream firewalls; 100Gbps spine links.

We want a recommendation for:
1) Minimal sustained GPU capacity to guarantee 95% of business-hour load without autoscaling.
2) Burst lane sizing (hot-pool) for handling peak spikes with graceful degradation.
3) Network lane reservations / NIC sizing per rack to avoid head-of-line blocking.
4) Operational checklist you need from our side to validate (telemetry, perf counters, example requests).

Priya from our systems integrator is looped in for network/ops data. Would appreciate an initial note with calculations we can review before a short workshop next week.

Thanks,
Alex

--
Alex Turner
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Systems
infra@acmesystems.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Acme VPC: initial throughput targets and network lanes

Alex — thanks for the clear brief and the attachments. I skimmed the CSV and the topology; there's enough to make a first-pass recommendation but we'll need a few runtime numbers from you (listed below) to lock sizing.

TL;DR proposal (first pass):
- Sustained pool (guaranteed): 40 GPUs (five racks of 8 GPUs) to cover median business-hour load with headroom.
- Burst / hot lane: additional 20 GPUs as a hot pool (can be on the same racks or burst to spare racks) to absorb short spikes up to 1.5x sustained for ~3–10 minute windows.
- Network: reserve 40Gbps per rack (NIC-level QoS) and a minimum of 2x100Gbps upstream aggregate to avoid link contention in spikes.

Requests / data we need from Acme to refine numbers: 
1) Real p95 latency per model on a single A100 (samples of 1k requests with raw timing).
2) Typical batching behavior (do you use request coalescing? typical batch sizes?).
3) KV cache hit rate for interactive calls (if prefix reuse, roughly %).
4) Expected growth curve over next 6 months (conservative/likely/optimistic).

Operational asks from Redwood side we will bring to the workshop:
- Capacity checklist (I attached mina-capacity-checklist.xlsx) — please fill and return.
- Suggested perf benchmarks we will run (microbench scripts and test harness).
- Autoscaling proposal: suggestion below (policy we think fits your spike profile).

Autoscale & graceful degradation idea: 
- Warm pool of 20 GPUs remaining parked but with warmed KV caches and model loaded (fast attach <60s).
- Reactive autoscale policy: expand by 10 GPUs when sustained 95th token/sec > required for 75% of capacity for 2 minutes; contract after 10 minutes below 50%.
- Fallback: if burst > hot pool and latency approaches SLO breach, degrade non-interactive routes (batch/analytics) first, then reduce max gen length on interactive flows.

I'll hand the sizing math to Rishi and ask him to produce a quick spreadsheet with assumptions. Let's schedule a 45-minute sync on Thursday 2026-08-06 at 1400 ET to go through numbers and the network diagram. Meeting link: https://meet.redwood.ai/j/mina-acme-capacity-0806

Thanks — Mina

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-02 13:21:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Acme VPC: initial throughput targets and network lanes

Folks — I ran a first-pass calc based on Alex's CSV and Mina's constraints. Below are assumptions and the resulting sizing bands; I attached rishi-sizing-estimates.csv with the row-level math.

Assumptions (conservative):
- Model: 35B decoder, mixed attention optimizations. Typical generation: 160 tokens; p95 length 512.
- GPU performance: measured in our lab for a similar 35B model on A100-80GB (FP16 w/ activation compression): per-GPU sustained generation throughput ~45–60 tokens/sec for seq_len=160 depending on batching. At seq_len=512 that falls to ~18–28 tokens/sec.
- Effective tokens/sec target (business-hour median): 75,000 tokens/min = 1250 tokens/sec. Peak short spikes up to 180,000 tokens/min = 3000 tokens/sec.
- Effective token distribution: roughly 80% of tokens at seq_len≈160, 20% at longer seqs. Use weighted harmonic mean to estimate per-GPU effective tokens/sec ≈ 40 tokens/sec.

Sizing math (rounded):
- Sustained capacity need = 1250 tokens/sec ÷ 40 tokens/sec per GPU ≈ 31 GPUs. Add operational headroom (25%) => 39 GPUs → round to 40 GPUs (5 racks of 8 GPUs).
- Hot/burst layer to absorb 3000 tokens/sec peak: 3000 ÷ 40 ≈ 75 GPUs total. Subtract the 40 sustained => ~35 GPUs additional. Add a safety margin for queueing/serialization => round to 40 GPUs. For practical placement we propose a hot pool of 20 GPUs local + ability to burst to another 20 GPUs in a remote rack within the same VPC.

Network sizing:
- Per token egress for model responses ~0.24 KB/token (including protocol overhead). For 3000 tokens/sec peak → ~720 KB/s ≈5.8 Mbps — trivial per se, but the dominant network requirement is NVLink / PCIe within rack and NIC contention during cache warmups and model loads.
- NIC recommendation: 100Gbps per rack will comfortably cover background syncs, model pulls, and cross-host fallback traffic. Reserve QoS lanes: 60% for inference, 20% for model sync/ops, 20% spare.

Operational notes and next steps:
1) Benchmark run: we need 1k sample requests from Acme (as Mina listed). I'll run the microbench against an identical 35B build to produce per-GPU p50/p95/p99 across seq lengths 128/256/512.
2) KV cache behavior: if your cache hit rate is >60% for interactive flows we can reduce effective required GPUs by ~15% due to prefix reuse—please provide measured cache statistics.
3) Warm pool strategy: preload model and run a short stream of synthetic traffic to warm KV caches and tokenizer caches; warm attach time target < 45s.
4) Cost/ops tradeoffs: if Acme is willing to accept quantized int8 variants for 20% of traffic (non-critical flows) we can cut GPU count by ~20% at the expense of a small quality delta.

I'll upload the raw spreadsheet. If the Acme numbers align with these lab perf figures, I agree with Mina's proposal of 40 sustained + 20 local hot + 20 remote-burst capacity (logical total 80 GPUs, physical starting point: 5 racks = 40 GPUs; reserve 3 racks as hot/burst).

-Rishi
